name: Tiles for Bathroom
description: Kostya is extremely busy: he is renovating his house! He needs to hand wallpaper, assemble furniture throw away trash. Kostya is buying tiles for bathroom today. He is standing in front of a large square stand with tiles in a shop. The stand is a square of $$$n \times n$$$ cells, each cell of which contains a small tile with color $$$c_{i,\,j}$$$. The shop sells tiles in packs: more specifically, you can only buy a subsquare of the initial square. A subsquare is any square part of the stand, i. e. any set $$$S(i_0, j_0, k) = \{c_{i,\,j}\ |\ i_0 \le i \lt i_0 + k, j_0 \le j \lt j_0 + k\}$$$ with $$$1 \le i_0, j_0 \le n - k + 1$$$. Kostya still does not know how many tiles he needs, so he considers the subsquares of all possible sizes. He doesn't want his bathroom to be too colorful. Help Kostya to count for each $$$k \le n$$$ the number of subsquares of size $$$k \times k$$$ that have at most $$$q$$$ different colors of tiles. Two subsquares are considered different if their location on the stand is different.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$q$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 1500$$$, $$$1 \le q \le 10$$$) — the size of the stand and the limit on the number of distinct colors in a subsquare. Each of the next $$$n$$$ lines contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$c_{i,\,j}$$$ ($$$1 \le c_{i,\,j} \le n^2$$$): the $$$j$$$-th integer in the $$$i$$$-th line is the color of the tile in the cell $$$(i,\,j)$$$.
output_specification: For each $$$k$$$ from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ print a single integer — the number of subsquares of size $$$k \times k$$$ with no more than $$$q$$$ different colors.
approach_summary: Exploit monotonicity of two-pointer invariant [L, R]. Advance R while shifting L forward to maintain validity, running in O(N) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1500D — Tiles for Bathroom [34. Two Pointers]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: When scanning contiguous subarrays or paired indices, advancing the right pointer $R$ monotonically tightens or relaxes the constraint, allowing the left pointer $L$ to only advance forward without ever needing to reset backwards.
